record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the hyperbolic Euler-Lagrange equations governing the time-dependent Skyrme model and its Faddeev submodel in 3+1 dimensions, can one establish a mathematical well-posedness theory and determine the qualitative behavior of time-dependent solutions, including existence, uniqueness, regularity, and dynamical behavior for finite-energy data?

evidence.quote: we remark that there has been no mathematical study on the well-posedness of either the system of equations (3.16) and (3.17) or the equation (3.19), both hyperbolic, nor any study on the behavior of the time-dependent solutions of these important equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the time-dependent Skyrme model on Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^{1+3}$ with metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$. The field is a map $U:\mathbb{R}^{1+3}\to SU(2)$, and the Lagrangian density is
$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Sk}}=\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(R_\mu R^\mu)+\tfrac{1}{16}\,\mathrm{tr}\big([R_\mu,R_\nu][R^\mu,R^\nu]\big),$$
where $R_\mu=U^{-1}\partial_\mu U$ takes values in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. The corresponding Euler–Lagrange equations form a quasilinear hyperbolic system for $U$.

Consider also the Faddeev submodel, in which the field is a map $\mathbf{n}:\mathbb{R}^{1+3}\to S^2\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, $|\mathbf{n}|=1$, with Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Fa}}=\tfrac{1}{2}\,\partial_\mu\mathbf{n}\cdot\partial^\mu\mathbf{n}-\tfrac{1}{4}\,F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu},\qquad F_{\mu\nu}=\mathbf{n}\cdot(\partial_\mu\mathbf{n}\times\partial_\nu\mathbf{n}),$$
whose Euler–Lagrange equation is a quasilinear hyperbolic equation for $\mathbf{n}$.

The associated conserved energies are
$$E_{\mathrm{Sk}}[U]=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\Big(-\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(R_iR_i)-\tfrac{1}{16}\mathrm{tr}([R_i,R_j][R_i,R_j])\Big)\,dx,$$
$$E_{\mathrm{Fa}}[\mathbf{n}]=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\Big(\tfrac{1}{2}\partial_i\mathbf{n}\cdot\partial_i\mathbf{n}+\tfrac{1}{4}F_{ij}F_{ij}\Big)\,dx,$$
which are finite for the relevant Cauchy data.

Establish a mathematical well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problems associated to these two hyperbolic systems with finite-energy initial data $(U,\partial_t U)|_{t=0}$ and $(\mathbf{n},\partial_t\mathbf{n})|_{t=0}$, including:
(a) local and global existence of solutions;
(b) uniqueness in a suitable class;
(c) regularity (propagation of Sobolev regularity, persistence of smoothness);
(d) qualitative dynamical behavior such as long-time asymptotics, scattering, stability of solitons, or singularity formation.
artifact.status_search_result: A general well-posedness theory for the full (3+1)-dimensional Skyrme and Faddeev hyperbolic Euler–Lagrange systems with arbitrary finite-energy data appears to remain open. Partial progress is available: Geba–Nakanishi–Rajeev and others established global existence and scattering for Skyrme wave maps with small critical data, and Li (Duke Math. J. 2021) proved global well-posedness for equivariant (hedgehog) solutions of the (3+1) Skyrme model with large data. No comparable general result has been reported for non-symmetric finite-energy Cauchy data, nor for the Faddeev submodel.

status_evidence.title: Global well-posedness of hedgehog solutions for the (3+1) Skyrme model
status_evidence.snippet: Considers hedgehog solutions in the (3+1)-dimensional Skyrme model and proves global well-posedness for arbitrarily large equivariant initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: global well-posedness is known for the equivariant hedgehog reduction of the (3+1) Skyrme model.

status_evidence.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for Skyrme wave maps
status_evidence.snippet: Proves global existence and scattering for equivariant generalizations of wave maps related to the Skyrme model with small critical data.
status_evidence.claim: Small-data global well-posedness and scattering results exist for Skyrme-type wave maps in 3+1 dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Waves in the Skyrme–Faddeev model and integrable reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies wave-type reductions of the (3+1)-dimensional Skyrme–Faddeev model via Whitham averaging, without establishing a general well-posedness theory.
status_evidence.claim: For the Faddeev submodel, only special reductions and formal wave analyses are available; a general well-posedness theory is not established.
